{
  "candidate_rtl": "`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none
module pw_crc32_d4 (
    input  wire [3:0] data_in,
    input  wire [31:0] state_in,
    output wire [3:0] data_out,
    output wire [31:0] state_out
);
    // Reflected Ethernet CRC polynomial, advanced by four bits.
    localparam [31:0] P0 = 32'hedb88320 >> 3;
    localparam [31:0] P1 = 32'hedb88320 >> 2;
    localparam [31:0] P2 = 32'hedb88320 >> 1;
    localparam [31:0] P3 = 32'hedb88320;

    // The low four polynomial bits are zero, so all four feedback
    // bits can be computed independently from the original inputs.
    wire [3:0] feedback;
    assign feedback = data_in ^ state_in[3:0];
    assign data_out = feedback;

    genvar n;
    generate
        for (n = 0; n < 32; n = n + 1) begin : bit_result
            localparam [3:0] MASK = {P3[n], P2[n], P1[n], P0[n]};
            localparam integer COUNT =
                ((MASK >> 0) & 1) + ((MASK >> 1) & 1) +
                ((MASK >> 2) & 1) + ((MASK >> 3) & 1);
            localparam [3:0] ONE = MASK & (~MASK + 4'b0001);
            wire shifted;
            if (n < 28) begin : original_state
                assign shifted = state_in[n+4];
            end else begin : zero_fill
                assign shifted = 1'b0;
            end

            if (COUNT == 0) begin : no_feedback
                assign state_out[n] = shifted;
            end else if (COUNT == 3) begin : balanced_three
                // Balance the state term with one feedback bit instead
                // of placing it after a three-feedback parity chain.
                wire pair_parity;
                wire state_parity;
                assign pair_parity = ^(feedback & (MASK ^ ONE));
                assign state_parity = shifted ^ (^(feedback & ONE));
                assign state_out[n] = pair_parity ^ state_parity;
            end else begin : other_feedback
                assign state_out[n] = shifted ^ (^(feedback & MASK));
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule
`default_nettype wire
",
  "bottleneck": "The baseline critical paths start at state_in[2] and traverse an input buffer followed by several mapped logic stages. Independently reducing expanded state/data masks can obscure the common data/state XORs and increase input loading and parity-network depth.",
  "rewrite": "Factor the transformation through four shared feedback bits, data_in XOR state_in[3:0]. Compute the reflected four-bit CRC update using constant shifted-polynomial masks. For outputs containing three feedback terms, balance the final parity as a two-feedback pair XOR a state/feedback pair. Preserve data_out explicitly as the four chronological feedback bits.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The intended maximum logical depth is three two-input XOR levels from a low state or data input, with reduced direct loading on those inputs. This should improve the opportunity to beat the baseline 0.82 ns arrival, but no numerical improvement is verified without the specified synthesis, mapping, and STA flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Requires four shared input XORs and constant-selected output parity networks; unused mask terms and zero-fill logic disappear during synthesis. No cells, buffers, or preservation attributes are forced. Mapped area and electrical compliance, including the 1318.514560 um2 cap, remain to be measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Complete combinational implementation of the parameterless pw_crc32_d4 top, with unchanged unsigned ports and no helper modules required. Uses the exact reflected CRC32 polynomial and four-bit processing order. Both outputs are defined for every binary data_in and arbitrary 32-bit state_in, without initialization, final inversion, assumptions, state, or added latency. Equivalence and implementation checks have not been run here."
